summary: Polk County, OR lookout station burned in a June 1931 timber fire; a 1963 cab was gone by 1968-1973, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 6x9 ft cab with trailer quarters (1963, per register and firelookout.com)
facts.status_note: 1931 lookout burned; 1963 cab removed (1968 per Forest Lookouts; gone by 1973 per the register and firelookout.com); no source describes remains at the site

events.note: Lookout station on Willamette Valley Lumber company land burned June 6, 1931; newspapers differ on destroyed versus burned and on timber losses

Ground cabin erected at the emergency lookout in 1963 at a cost of $404.16 per Forest Lookouts; register and firelookout.com describe a 1963 6x9 ft cab with trailer quarters (the sources do not say they are the same structure)
Forest Lookouts says the lookout was removed in 1968
Register and firelookout.com say the cab was gone by 1973; conflicts with the 1968 removal date
Registered November 15, 2010, nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: Daily Capital Journal: fire destroyed about three million feet of logs and the lookout station
evidence.quote: destroyed about three million feet of felled logs and the Riley's Peak Lookout station

evidence.supports: Sunday Oregonian: lookout reported destroyed; 3,000,000 feet of logs reported damaged
evidence.quote: A lookout station there was reported destroyed, and 3,000,000 feet of logs were reported damaged.

evidence.supports: fire swept over about 1,000 acres of cut-over land
evidence.quote: swept over approximately 1000 acres of cut-over land

evidence.supports: Forest Log: the cabin burned in a forest fire on June 6
evidence.quote: Reports received from the Polk county unit recently are to the effect that the Rileys Peak lookout cabin was burned in a forest fire on June 6.

evidence.supports: Forest Log: company losses about two million feet of logs
evidence.quote: the losses to the company were limited to approximately two million feet of logs

evidence.supports: lookout station was property of the Polk County Fire Patrol association
evidence.quote: The lookout station was the property of the Polk County Fire Patrol association.

evidence.supports: 1963 cab and trailer quarters erected, gone by 1973 (register)
evidence.quote: In 1963, a 6'x9' cab and trailer quarters were erected, which were gone by 1973.

evidence.supports: firelookout.com: 1963 6x9 cab and trailer quarters; gone 1973

evidence.quote: 1963: A ground cabin was constructed at this emergency lookout at a cost of $404.16.

evidence.supports: costs paid from state restoration funds after loss of Fanno Mountain Lookout in the Columbus Day Storm
evidence.quote: These costs were paid from the state restoration funds from the loss of Fanno Mountain Lookout the year before in the Columbus Day Storm.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts: the lookout was removed in 1968
14 miles west of Dallas, Polk County
administered by the Oregon Dept. of Forestry
Sunday Oregonian item dated June 7, 1931 (fire on Willamette Valley Lumber company property)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says the ground cab was removed in 1968; the register and firelookout.com say it was gone by 1973. The story reports both dates and does not pick one.
Newspaper items quoted by Forest Lookouts gave about three million feet of logs; The Forest Log gave about two million feet. The story gives both figures.

notes_for_editor: All 1931 newspaper material is quoted secondhand on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspapers were not read (Historic Oregon Newspapers would confirm June 1931 items). The orww.org PDF of the Forest Lookouts page is a print of that same page, so it is not counted as a separate source. The 1963 cab's removal year is the main open question. No source describes the site today.
